newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: BEAZLEY SAYS HOWARD DIDN'T INVENT FREEDOM OF SPEECH
Federal Opposition leader Kim Beazley has dismissed John Howard's claim that freedom of speech has improved under the coalition government, as a bit of Prime Ministerial hubris.
Mr Howard says the pall of censorship on certain issues has now been lifted, so people no longer have to live in fear of being branded as a racist or bigot.
But Mr Beazley says Australia has had freedom of speech for more than a century, and claims Mr Howard has missed the point.
Mr Beazley says freedom of speech wasn't something invented by John Howard six months ago.
VANSTONE ACCUSED OF NOT UNDERSTANDING ROLE OF UNIS
The National Tertiary Education Union says Universities have always been at the forefront of change.
In a speech to university adminsitrators in Sydney today, Federal Education minister Amanda Vanstone called on universities to adapt to changes and not look to the Government for answers.
The minister also accused students and vice-chancellors of creating a climate of misinformation about the effect of cuts to universities, saying it was damaging the sector.
But Union President, Carolyn Allport, says Senator Vanstone thinks the best way to achieve change is by reducing funding, and accused her of not understanding the role of universities.
OPPOSITION SAYS EMPLOYMENT CHANGES WILL CREATE GHETTOS
The Federal Shadow Employment Minister, Martin Ferguson, says the Government's employment, education and training plans will lead to a nation of haves and have nots.
Martin Ferguson says the plans could force poor and low paid people into ghettos. Mr Ferguson was in Launceston, in Tasmania, this morning, where he met a group of hospitality apprentices.
He says the group was disturbed by the prospect of a low youth wage and what they saw as a lack of support for training, with cuts to Skillshare programmes.
AUSTRALIAN OIL STOCKS SEEN "DECLINING FAST"
The author of a new book on oil says the rate of consumption of oil in Australia is outstripping the rate of discovery by three to one.

Brian Fleay, who's the author of "The Decline of the Age of Oil", says Australian and global oil production will soon begin to decline. But Mr Fleay says the decline in Australia will be far quicker than the global rate.
He says this means Australian governments need to urgently rethink transport policies to reduce the reliance on the car.
GOVERNMENT WARNED ON GLOBAL WARNING
Australia's peak medical group has warned that heat related deaths are likely to rise, due to global warming.
The Australian Medical Association says it's disappointed with the Federal Government's attitude towards the problem, and action is needed now, because it could be too late in five years.
AMA Federal President, Keith Woollard, told a conference co-sponsored by the AMA and Greenpeace that global warming will lead to a rise in infectious diseases, and malnutrition.
Scientists at the conference believe the earth's average temperature may rise by three degrees over the next century, playing havoc with crops.
The AMA says its alliance with Greenpeace on global warming sends a message to Government on the urgent need for action.
SIX JAILED FOR STABBING ABORIGINE
Jail sentences have been handed to six non-Aboriginal men who carried out a revenge attack after an assault by a group of Aborigines.
Alice Springs Magistrate, Warren Donald, told the court that although the men denied the plan was racially motivated, they were of European descent, and the victim was Aboriginal.
The men had planned to find six Aboriginal men who'd been involved in an assault a week earlier, and had set off with another man who, unknown to them, was carrying a knife.
This man stabbed a young Aboriginal man who'd had nothing to do with the attack the previous week.
Five of the men have been sentenced to six months jail, while the sixth was given a suspended sentence.
ROOS MOVING IN TO TOWNSVILLE GARDENS

Dry weather in north Queensland's west has led to a new kind of urban drift. The Environment Department says residents in the western suburbs of Townsville are becoming accustomed to seeing kangaroos grazing in their gardens.
But the new arrivals are taking some time to adjust to city life - Senior Wildlife Officer Mike Pople says many have been killed or injured by dogs or vehicles.
MISSING MAN'S BOAT FOUND IN CROCODILE AREA
Police searching for a man missing in a crocodile infested area off Western Australia's Kimberley coast have located his aluminium dinghy anchored on a beach.
Police say tracks can be seen leading to a nearby tree, and a helicopter has now joined the search for 42-year old Trevor Durber, from Wyndham.
Mr Durber was reported missing last night.
